# Autopsy: BANK-INTEREST-1978

## Section 1: EARS Requirements

### Req 1 — Vampire (unbounded accumulator / buffer growth)
- WHEN the loop spanning `POST-MONTH`, `POST-UNTIL-TARGET`, `MAIN-PARA.UNTIL-24`, `POST-YEAR.TIMES-34` iterates, THE SYSTEM SHALL bound `WS-ITER` by an explicit guard so that it cannot grow without limit.
- IF `WS-ITER` reaches the guard limit, THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL exit the loop and record the bound in the autopsy.
- WHEN the healed IR is rescanned, THE SYSTEM SHALL report zero Vampire findings for `WS-ITER`.

### Req 2 — Ghost (unreachable code)
- WHEN the lifter emits code for `BANK-INTEREST-1978`, THE SYSTEM SHALL omit block `AUDIT-TRAIL.42` because no CFG path from the entry reaches it.
- WHEN the healed module is compared with the reference interpreter, THE SYSTEM SHALL report 100 percent parity, since removed code never executed.
- WHEN the healed IR is rescanned, THE SYSTEM SHALL report zero Ghost findings for `AUDIT-TRAIL.42`.

## Section 2: Patch Proposals

### Patch 1 — Vampire in `POST-UNTIL-TARGET.39` (line 39)
`WS-ITER` only grows inside the loop and no exit condition reads it; it will silently wrap past 10^5.
Add a cap guard at the end of `POST-UNTIL-TARGET.39` (line 39):

```cobol
       ADD 1 TO WS-ITER.
       IF WS-ITER > 100000
           MOVE WS-TARGET TO WS-BALANCE
           DISPLAY "WS-ITER CAP HIT AT " WS-ITER
       END-IF.
```

This makes the existing `WS-BALANCE >= WS-TARGET` exit reachable on inputs where COMP-3 truncation drives monthly interest to zero, preventing silent wrap and giving the healer a rescan target of zero Vampires.

### Patch 2 — Ghost in `AUDIT-TRAIL.42` (line 42)
Block `AUDIT-TRAIL.42` has no incoming CFG edge; nothing performs, calls, or jumps to it.
The intended `PERFORM AUDIT-TRAIL` was dropped from `MAIN-PARA`. Either restore the `PERFORM`:

```cobol
           PERFORM AUDIT-TRAIL
           STOP RUN.
```

or delete the paragraph entirely if the audit trail is no longer required. Deleting is the safe default since the code never ran; restoring the `PERFORM` is only correct if the audit output is still wanted.
